prose_overlay.tldr: One law-independent sequential algorithm, not using \(s\) or \(r\), attains for every fixed smoothness pair the constructive log-free upper rate \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-1-2r/(2r+d)}\) in the unrestricted oracle-subtracted excess-MSE decision problem. If one and the same known allocation, independent of the law and both smoothness indices, is pointwise oracle-optimal throughout the union of model classes, a smoothness-agnostic AIPW construction attains the sharper mean-only upper rate \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\). Equal conditional variance and pointwise singleton-support weights furnish such allocations. These are upper results: no positive centered converse over all measurable, possibly biased estimators, and hence no exact causal minimax order, is claimed.
prose_overlay.related_work: Li and Simchi-Levi, \cite{LiSimchiLevi2026SequentialEfficiency}, Definition 2.1, motivate the law-independent non-anticipating design class. Their Section 4.4 upper theorem has logarithmic slack, and their converse quantifies over an unbiased estimator pair; its exact-centering projection does not settle oracle-subtracted MSE for arbitrary biased estimators. The present fixed-smoothness and smoothness-agnostic constructions remove logarithmic loss on the upper side only. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han, \cite{ShenGaoWittenHan2020Variance}, and Wang, Brown, Cai, and Levine, \cite{WangBrownCaiLevine2008MeanVariance}, explain why variance learning with an unknown rough mean requires explicit treatment. Cai and Wang, \cite{CaiWang2008AdaptiveVariance}, study adaptive variance estimation with logarithmic slack in a different regression experiment; here held-out finite-library selection is absorbed at the causal second-order scale. Li and Owen, \cite{LiOwen2024BatchDML}, and Kato, Ishihara, Honda, and Narita, \cite{KatoIshiharaHondaNarita2020AdaptiveATE}, provide first-order predictable cross-fitting and AIPW precedents. Brown and Low, \cite{BrownLow1996ConstrainedRisk}, and Duchi and Ruan, \cite{DuchiRuan2021ConstrainedRisk}, motivate bias-robust lower-bound tools but do not calculate the adaptive law-dependent oracle subtraction. That centered Bayes problem remains open; smoothness adaptation of the upper construction does not.
prose_overlay.interpretation: The two-nuisance display is an achievable second-order law, not a minimax equality. Mean error enters through the predictable AIPW variance remainder, whereas variance error enters through regret from learning the generalized Neyman allocation. When the same oracle allocation is known and valid for every law and every smoothness class under consideration, allocation regret is identically zero and only the mean rate remains. Smoothness knowledge is unnecessary for these upper conclusions because the held-out selection penalty \(m^{-1}\log\log m\) is asymptotically smaller than every fixed Hölder risk \(m^{-2u/(2u+d)}\).
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The proofs retain conditional Gaussianity, fixed positive overlap, and fixed \(n\)-independent Hölder classes. The smoothness-adaptive theorem gives one algorithm for every fixed \(s,r>0\), but its constants and threshold need not be uniform over smoothness. The sharper mean-only theorem additionally requires one known allocation, independent of \(P\), \(s\), and \(r\), that is pointwise oracle-optimal simultaneously across the union of classes served by that algorithm. Gaussianity supplies exponential-moment control for residual-square learning and held-out selection; no non-Gaussian extension, leading minimax constant, vanishing-overlap theory, unrestricted centered converse, or variance-driven converse under merely bounded weights is proved.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The proved contribution is a constructive log-free upper bound for the unrestricted sequential oracle-subtracted excess-MSE problem, including one smoothness-agnostic law-independent algorithm that attains the stated rate for every fixed \(s,r>0\). The paper also proves the standalone nuisance maximum under active-region and strict-range conditions and its one-dimensional refinements. If a single known allocation is simultaneously oracle-optimal over every law and smoothness class covered by the algorithm---as in the retained equal-variance and pointwise singleton-support corollaries---the achievable rate sharpens to \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\). There is no positive lower bound for the unrestricted centered criterion, no causal minimax equality, and no exact all-regime frontier. The centered Bayes-risk converse and allocation-sensitive lower theory when \(r<s\) remain open; smoothness adaptation of the upper construction is settled.

project_justification.gap: Li and Simchi-Levi's second-order upper result retains logarithmic slack, while its converse is stated for exactly unbiased estimators and uses an exact-centering excess-variance identity that does not settle oracle-subtracted mean-squared error for arbitrary biased estimators at the second-order scale. Existing adaptive variance-estimation results also do not directly yield a log-free sequential causal excess-risk theorem.
project_justification.niche: The decision problem fixes one law-independent non-anticipating design and one unrestricted observed-path estimator before the supremum over the Hölder law. Its upper theory must control expected allocation regret and predictable AIPW regression error without epochwise logarithmic losses. Its lower theory must preserve the law-dependent subtraction \(V^*(P)/n\) inside an unrestricted Bayes-risk calculation.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves fixed-smoothness and smoothness-agnostic log-free upper constructions, reduces the achievable rate to standalone mean and variance risks, and identifies a sharper mean-only regime whenever one known allocation is simultaneously oracle-optimal across all smoothness classes served by the algorithm. The unrestricted centered converse remains the precisely stated posterior-variance problem; smoothness adaptation of the upper construction is settled.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The fixed-smoothness witness uses predictable clipped local-polynomial mean regression and residual-square variance regression. The smoothness-agnostic witness uses fixed ordered training and validation folds, finite dyadic local-polynomial libraries, held-out inverse-propensity empirical-risk selection, clipping, and expected-risk geometric summation. In the known common-oracle-allocation regime, variance learning is omitted and only the selected outcome-regression fits enter the predictable AIPW score.
sampling_model.design: A law-independent sequence \(D=(q_t^D)_{t=1}^n\in\mathfrak D_{n,\varepsilon}\) of measurable positive non-anticipating kernels is fixed before \(P\). The general adaptive upper algorithm uses geometric epochs and freezes selected fits before later assignments. In the law-invariant-allocation theorem, one and the same known allocation \(e\), independent of \(P\), \(s\), and \(r\), is used from the start and is assumed pointwise oracle-optimal simultaneously throughout the union of model classes under consideration.

prop:oracle-identification.justification: This proposition separates the causal target from its observed-data identifying functional and fixes the oracle first-order variance benchmark.
prop:oracle-identification.gap: No new identification claim is made beyond the known randomized-design functional and efficient influence function.
prop:oracle-identification.consumer: Every excess-risk statement subtracts this same explicitly defined benchmark.

lem:predictable-aipw-holder-upper.justification: This lemma gives the explicit fixed-smoothness predictable design and estimator underlying the constructive upper bound.
lem:predictable-aipw-holder-upper.gap: It is an upper witness only and does not establish a centered lower bound over unrestricted estimators.
lem:predictable-aipw-holder-upper.consumer: The explicit Hölder theorem and nuisance-risk reduction use this fixed-bandwidth witness; the separate adaptive theorem removes its dependence on known smoothness.

thm:nuisance-reduction-frontier.justification: This is the evaluable nuisance-risk form of the constructive log-free upper result under the active-region and strict-range conditions.
thm:nuisance-reduction-frontier.gap: The comparison is one-sided; it does not show the nuisance maximum is unavoidable for biased estimators.
thm:nuisance-reduction-frontier.consumer: The result separates attainable causal excess risk into standalone mean and variance learning problems.

lem:variance-risk-absorption.justification: The lemma derives the standalone nuisance scales without claiming an unsupported exact variance-function exponent.
lem:variance-risk-absorption.gap: Strict variance range is necessary for its variance lower submodel.
lem:variance-risk-absorption.consumer: It converts the causal upper result into explicit Hölder exponents.

thm:explicit-holder-frontier.justification: This theorem states the direct log-free Hölder upper law furnished by the explicit predictable design and estimator.
thm:explicit-holder-frontier.gap: No positive unrestricted oracle-subtracted lower bound is proved.
thm:explicit-holder-frontier.consumer: ATE, weighted-ATE, subgroup, and fixed-policy experiments obtain a concrete fixed-smoothness achievable rate.

thm:one-dimensional-explicit-frontier.justification: This theorem concerns standalone nuisance risks and their exact maximum only.
thm:one-dimensional-explicit-frontier.gap: The Shen--Gao--Witten--Han result is used only for an upper bound under the present density class.
thm:one-dimensional-explicit-frontier.consumer: Scalar-covariate studies can select nuisance resolution without inferring an unsupported causal equivalence.

prop:rough-mean-absorption.justification: This is a direct algebraic identity among three exponents.
prop:rough-mean-absorption.consumer: It explains the exact maximum in the rough-mean regime.

prop:smooth-mean-reduction.justification: This is the direct algebraic smoothness-threshold identity.
prop:smooth-mean-reduction.consumer: It identifies when the joint variance upper exponent equals the known-mean exponent.

lem:shen-random-design-variance-upper.justification: This cited leaf supplies only the published univariate variance upper bound.
lem:shen-random-design-variance-upper.gap: Its lower construction is not imported into the bounded-below density class.
lem:shen-random-design-variance-upper.consumer: The univariate transfer lemma uses its estimator rate.

lem:shen-upper-transfer.justification: This lemma transfers the sourced univariate upper bound through constant known weights.
lem:shen-upper-transfer.gap: It proves no equivalence and no causal statement.
lem:shen-upper-transfer.consumer: The one-dimensional nuisance theorem uses it for the upper side of \(\mathsf Q_n^{\sigma}\).

lem:single-arm-variance-obstruction.justification: This explicit admissible target makes the oracle allocation known while variance estimation remains nonparametrically hard.
lem:single-arm-variance-obstruction.gap: It refutes a universal variance-driven converse but does not settle allocation-sensitive multi-arm targets.
lem:single-arm-variance-obstruction.consumer: The causal frontier omits the variance lower scale when \(r<s\) under the frozen weight conditions.

oeq:unrestricted-centered-converse.justification: This records the remaining posterior-variance calculation needed for a positive lower bound over all measurable, possibly biased estimators.
oeq:unrestricted-centered-converse.gap: The law-dependent oracle benchmark must be canceled inside the Bayes calculation at second order; total-risk testing bounds do not accomplish this.
oeq:unrestricted-centered-converse.consumer: A positive or negative solution would determine whether any proved upper rate is unavoidable under the unrestricted centered criterion. This question is separate from the variance-driven allocation-sensitivity converse when \(r<s\); smoothness adaptation of the upper construction is settled by \(\text{thm:smoothness-adaptive-log-free-upper}\).

thm:smoothness-adaptive-log-free-upper.justification: This theorem settles upper-side smoothness adaptation: one law-independent algorithm not using \(s\) or \(r\) attains the fixed-smoothness log-free rate for every fixed smoothness pair.
thm:smoothness-adaptive-log-free-upper.gap: The constants are not uniform over smoothness, Gaussianity is retained, and no centered converse is supplied.
thm:smoothness-adaptive-log-free-upper.consumer: An experimenter can use one predictable procedure without knowing the Hölder orders while retaining the displayed second-order upper rate.

thm:law-invariant-oracle-allocation-uppe.justification: This theorem isolates the structural regime in which one common known oracle allocation works simultaneously across laws and smoothness classes, so allocation learning is unnecessary and the variance-smoothness term vanishes from the upper rate.
thm:law-invariant-oracle-allocation-uppe.gap: It is conditional on a single allocation independent of \(P\), \(s\), and \(r\), and it remains an upper result without a centered converse.
thm:law-invariant-oracle-allocation-uppe.consumer: The equal-variance and pointwise singleton-support corollaries use the same smoothness-agnostic mean-only construction.

prop:known-variance-mean-only-upper.justification: Equal variance bounds force the entire variance function to be known, making the standalone weighted-variance risk zero and the oracle allocation law-invariant.
prop:known-variance-mean-only-upper.gap: The proposition does not imply a matching centered causal lower bound.
prop:known-variance-mean-only-upper.consumer: Experiments with known common conditional variance can omit variance learning and use the mean-only upper rate.

prop:singleton-support-mean-only-upper.justification: With exactly one weighted arm at each covariate, the positivity-constrained optimizer is determined by support alone and is independent of unknown variances.
prop:singleton-support-mean-only-upper.gap: The condition is structural and pointwise; no comparable simplification is asserted for overlapping weighted supports.
prop:singleton-support-mean-only-upper.consumer: Pointwise single-arm policy-value targets can use the known allocation and the mean-only upper rate.
